title: Treatment of post-traumatic stress disorder with medical nitrous oxide combined with exposure to a personal traumatic script: a multicenter randomized controlled trial
official: Treatment of post-traumatic stress disorder with medical nitrous oxide combined with exposure to a personal traumatic script: a multicenter randomized controlled trial (POTESTA)
summary: Main objective: To investigate the therapeutic efficacy of medical nitrous oxide versus medical air, combined with reading a personal traumatic script on the progression of PTSD symptoms, using the CAPS-5 structured interview (Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5), between the initial assessment (D0), prior to the start of treatment (4 weekly treatment sessions) and the follow-up assessment 3 months after the end of treatment.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age: from 18 to 65 years old
2. Nature of the traumatic event: interpersonal violence, including sexual, physical and psychological abuse
3. Patient with PTSD who has failed to respond to at least one therapeutic approach, psychotherapy, or treatment with an SSRI (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor)
4. PTSD as defined by the DSM-5, with symptoms present for more than 6 months (> 6 months)
5. CAPS-5 score ≥ 35
6. Participant who can receive MEOPA or medical oxygen through a face mask
7. French-speaking participant
8. Enrolled in the Social Security system
9. Having signed the informed consent form
10. A ‘suitable’ method of contraception for women of childbearing age
Exclusion criteria:
1. Addiction disorders/history of addiction; severe depression and/or severe anxiety that are not stabilised; psychotic, bipolar, dissociative identity or eating disorders; obsessive-compulsive disorder that is not stabilised; primary or severe Axis II disorders
2. Pregnancy and/or breastfeeding
3. Patients under legal guardianship and/or other circumstances rendering the patient unable to understand the nature, purpose, or consequences of the study
4. Contraindications to the use of medical nitrous oxide and any condition in which air is trapped inside the body and its expansion could be dangerous: pneumothorax, emphysema, intestinal obstruction, intracranial hypertension, known and untreated vitamin B12 or B9 deficiency (based on a test performed within the last month), Patients requiring ventilation with pure oxygen; any impairment of consciousness preventing patient cooperation; head trauma; gas embolism; diving accident; Abdominal gas distension; Patients who have recently received an ophthalmic gas (SF6, C3F8, C2F6) used in eye surgery (as long as a gas bubble persists inside the eye and for a minimum period of 3 months); recent and non-recent neurological abnormalities
5. Subphysiological plasma concentrations of vitamin B12 or B9 (below the lower limit of the reference range)
6. Supraphysiological plasma concentrations of homocysteine (above the upper limit of the reference range)
7. Risk of suicide with a C-SSRS (Columbian-Suicide Severity Rating Scale) score of 4 or more
8. Treatments that may bias the study results
9. Ongong psychothérapy
